correctness.rationale: For a finite mutually singular probability tuple, the coordinate form of a projection and the total-variation norm of disjoint-band combinations give ||I-P||=1+max_x sum_j|g_j(x)| by the finite-rank Daugavet identity. Norm two requires each g_j to equal one on its full topological support and all other coefficient functions to vanish there, so the supports must be disjoint; disjoint continuous cutoffs give the converse. The norm-one measurable-band projection on the measure dual and the known Daugavet duality give infimum two, also verified directly by disjoint compact approximation and inversion of a near-identity moment matrix. Singularity is a dense G_delta by lower semicontinuity of total variation; independent classical dense-G_delta properties of nonatomic full-support probabilities give nonattainment as a comeagre phenomenon. For Lebesgue measure and delta at zero, the integral of min(Lx,1+epsilon) yields the Lipschitz lower bound, while explicit tent and ramp functions achieve defect 2/(2t-1) with Lipschitz growth t+ t/(2t-1). The 11,000 exact rational diagnostics verify only finite instances of this explicit construction. No finite experiment supplies the general proof.

originality.rationale: The exact numerical projection constant two follows from the previously published Daugavet duality theorem and is credited rather than claimed new. The present combined result identifies the precise topological-support condition for attaining that endpoint across arbitrary finite tuples of positive mutually singular probabilities, establishes dense but meagre attainment versus generic nonattainment within the natural measure-tuple parameter space, and proves a quantitative inverse-error regularity law for explicit near-minimizers. The recent codimension-two nonattainment constructions available for comparison have projection constants strictly larger than two. Distinct weak-star minimal-projection examples do not imply this support criterion or its quantitative instance. Broad contractive-projection theory may still contain an equivalent criterion, so publication priority is qualified; a failed search is not proof of novelty.
residual_risks: A broader previously published characterization of weak-star-continuous norm-one projections onto measure spans may subsume the support criterion through implication rather than matching words.

value.rationale: The natural endpoint of finite-codimensional projection theory requires distinguishing an infimum's value from actual minimizer existence. Across all finite codimensions for a broad positive-measure annihilator class, a complete topological-support criterion describes exactly when the lowest constant two is attained; genericity is the opposite of dense attainability, showing measurable singularity does not substitute for topological separation. The Lebesgue/evaluation example quantifies the necessary ill-conditioning of near-minimizers by a sharp inverse-defect exponent with explicit constructions. This is more than a known numerical-value corollary or isolated arbitrary invariant and motivates future analyses of minimal projections and regularity thresholds.
